messages:
Alex: quick question — we keep getting customer tickets where their app sees a 429 and treats it as a permanent limit. should the SDK map 429 -> RateLimitError and 503 -> TransientCapacityError, or is that too prescriptive?
Priya: I think mapping helps, but we also need to expose a short hint so frontend UIs can show a helpful CTA (retry vs contact sales). maybe an error class header?
Jon: +1 to header. propose `X-Redwood-Error-Class: rate_limit|capacity|auth` and `Retry-After` for delay. that way SDKs can do heuristic retry/backoff.
Marta: also want to capture routing reason for telemetry. e.g. `X-Redwood-Routing-Reason: node_overload` vs `routing_policy:cost_due_to_quota` so console can show why fallback happened.
Alex: good. on Console UX, do we surface different badge colors? customers get confused when a request 'succeeds' but was routed to a cheaper quantized variant. i want a small inline badge: "routed -> quantized" with hover text.
Priya: agree. badges should be non-alarming. maybe use neutral amber for degraded-perf and green for transparent routing. also we need a changelog entry for rollout that says: "Model B served due to high queue".
Jon: telemetry needs discrete fields (not free text) so we can alert on spikes. suggest fields: `error_code` (HTTP), `error_class` (our enum), `routing_variant` (string), `quota_type` (burst|sustained), `fallback_reason`.
Marta: customer-facing messages: keep them short. examples: 429 -> "Rate limit exceeded — retry after Xs"; 503 -> "Service busy — try again shortly". avoid exposing internal names like `node-overloaded-82`.
Alex: runtime/infra question — when we fallback to a cheaper model, should the primary HTTP response still be 200 and include `X-Redwood-Model-Variant` header, or return 206/302-like status to indicate partial fulfillment?
Priya: prefer 200 with header + structured metadata in response body. many clients assume non-2xx = error. better to be explicit: `model_variant` and `model_quality_score` fields.
Jon: agree. but SDKs should also surface an event (e.g., `onFallback`) so apps can log or surface a toast. console can map those events back to routes.
Marta: small security note — don't leak SLA tiers in client messages. e.g. avoid "your dedicated pool is empty". instead: "capacity constrained, request queued".
Alex: ok, action items: 1) Priya to draft header enums + error_class list; 2) Jon to add telemetry fields to event schema; 3) Marta to mock badge copy for Console; 4) I'll add SDK onFallback hook RFC.
Priya: putting a quick snippet for headers we can start with:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
X-Redwood-Error-Class: rate_limit
X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-Routing-Reason: capacity_pool_burst
```
Jon: looks good. one more: `X-Redwood-Client-Hint: quota_threshold_80pct` so frontend can optionally dim a button when close to quota.
Marta: +1. also for telemetry tags, we should annotate `route_id` and `model_id` to tie back to console dashboards.
Alex: deploy-bot FYI: once we land headers + SDK changes, can we roll feature flag gated?
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout: feature/error-headers v1 -> canary 10% tomorrow 03:00 UTC, full rollout 48h if no regressions. :rocket:
Priya: I'll open the PR with the header enums and add unit tests for SDK mapping.
Jon: I'll update the event schema doc and add an example query for Datadog to surface rate_limit spikes.
Marta: I'll add the badge designs to the Console board and write copy variations.
Alex: thanks team. let's sync if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
